acceptance: `omnexx run --sandbox docker --plan-only` starts the docker sandbox path (or fails fast with a clear docker-unavailable error); `--sandbox bogus` prints a UsageError; `--sandbox host` behavior unchanged
steps: In run.ts, pass the flag value through to run config as 'host' | 'docker' instead of casting to 'host'; reject any other value with a UsageError naming the flag
Add a pre-flight check: when docker is selected, verify the docker daemon is reachable before the plan starts and fail fast with install instructions if not
Keep OMNEXX_SANDBOX env and omnexx.toml [sandbox] as fallbacks with precedence flag > env > config
Add a unit test asserting --sandbox docker reaches the run config as 'docker' and --sandbox bogus exits with a UsageError
tests: test/unit/cli/run-flags.test.ts: docker passes through, bogus value rejected, host unchanged
title: Honor --sandbox docker instead of silently dropping it to host
why: Verified bug: run.ts:70 casts the flag to 'host' (`sandbox: f.sandbox as 'host'`), so `omnexx run --sandbox docker` runs unsandboxed with no warning. The docker sandbox is a headline safety feature for unattended runs and the config schema already accepts docker (schema.ts:441). A user who thinks they are sandboxed is not.

acceptance: `omnexx diff --json`, `omnexx checkpoints --json`, and `omnexx report --json` each print parseable JSON whose fields match the human-readable output; invalid run id still errors
steps: Register --json on diff, checkpoints, and report in program.ts

In inspect.ts, emit the same data each command already computes as JSON: diff (files changed + per-file hunks or a compact summary), checkpoints (id, commit, time, tests, spend), report (the REPORT.md fields)
Reuse the existing JSON output helper used by status/plan so formatting and error shape match
Add tests asserting valid JSON output, identical content to the human output, and that --json without a run still errors cleanly
tests: test/unit/cli/inspect-json.test.ts (new): JSON parses, fields match human output, bad run id errors
title: Add --json to diff, checkpoints, and report
why: status, plan, runs, facts, and doctor all support --json, but diff, checkpoints, and report do not, so scripts and the VS Code extension cannot consume them. These three are the natural machine-readable companions to status/plan for run inspection and reporting.

acceptance: `omnexx update --check` prints current vs latest and exits 0; up-to-date prints 'already on latest'; active run blocks upgrade with a clear message
steps: Create commands/update.ts with a register() function (extra-registrar pattern, auto-registered via extra/index.ts) exposing `omnexx update` with --check (report only) and --yes (skip confirm)
Use the existing checkForUpdate/isNewer helpers against the installed version; print current, latest, and a one-line changelog link
On upgrade, run the package-manager reinstall for the detected install method (npm -g) and print the new version; never upgrade mid-run (refuse if a run is active in this folder)
Export the new registrar from extra/index.ts and add tests for check-only output, up-to-date case, and refusal during an active run
tests: test/unit/cli/update-command.test.ts (new): check-only output, up-to-date, blocked-during-run; existing update-check.test.ts stays green
title: Add omnexx update: self-update check and upgrade
why: W15 TODO and a gap vs Claude Code/OpenCode, which self-update. checkForUpdate/isNewer already exist as helpers (update-check.ts) with tests, but no command exposes them, so users never learn a new version exists.

acceptance: Hovering a user message shows edit-and-resend; hovering an assistant message shows retry; retry replaces the previous assistant response; edit loads text into the composer
steps: In render.ts, add retry (assistant messages) and edit-and-resend (user messages) buttons to the existing msg-actions row, reusing the copy button's styling and hover behavior
In chat.ts, wire retry to re-send the last user message to chat-server and edit-and-resend to load the message text back into the composer with the original turn marked superseded
Keep the log capped at MAX_LOG_LINES=400 and ensure a retried turn replaces (not duplicates) the failed assistant response in the feed
Add render tests asserting the buttons appear on the right message types and are absent on system/act entries
tests: test/unit/vscode-chat-render.test.ts: buttons present per message type, absent on system entries
title: Per-message retry and edit-and-resend on user messages
why: Cline and Claude Code both let you retry a turn or edit and resend a message; omnexx's panel only has copy on hover. Retrying a bad turn is the single most common recovery action during a run, and today it requires retyping the whole message.

acceptance: New test file covers ratchet up/down/unchanged, skip paths, and pass/fail outcomes; all tests pass under test:quick
steps: Write tests for the ratchet: new failure fails the gate, known failure count going up fails, count going down passes, empty baseline passes
Cover gate outcomes for pass, fail, and skip paths including the spec-test skip rules
Use only in-memory fixtures, no real test runner invocation
Keep the tests fast (no timeouts) so they run in test:quick
tests: test/unit/core/spec-gate.test.ts (new): ratchet up/down/unchanged, skip rules, pass/fail outcomes
title: Unit tests for the spec gate ratchet
why: The spec gate is the product's central safety claim (no new failures, known-failure count can't go up) and it has no direct unit tests, only integration coverage via spec-tests.test.ts. A regression here silently weakens every run's guarantees.

acceptance: Each cheat pattern is detected with a message naming file and rule; legitimate edits pass; suite runs in test:quick
steps: Write tests for each detection: deleted test file, added .skip/.only, added @ts-ignore, snapshot rewrite, protected-file edit
Cover the negative cases: legitimate test edits and refactors must not trip the detector
Use small in-memory diffs/fixtures, no git or filesystem access
Assert the violation messages name the offending file and rule
tests: test/unit/verify/anticheat.test.ts (new): one case per cheat pattern plus negative cases
title: Unit tests for anti-cheat detection
why: Anti-cheat (deleted tests, .skip/.only, @ts-ignore, snapshot rewrites, protected-file edits) is the other half of the safety claim and also has no direct unit tests. Cheating the gate is the easiest way for a worker to fake progress.

acceptance: Backoff bounds, outage notification timing, give-up timing, abort, and success-after-retry are all asserted; no real timers or network
steps: Write tests with a fake clock and a stubbed failing function: backoff grows within baseDelayMs/maxDelayMs, outage notification fires after outageNotifyMs, give-up fires after giveUpAfterMs
Cover AbortSignal cancellation (StopRequested) and the ProvidersUnavailable error path
Cover success-after-retries returning the value with the right attempt count
No network, no timers: fake clock only
tests: test/unit/providers/retry.test.ts (new): backoff bounds, outage notify, give-up, abort, success-after-retry
title: Unit tests for provider retry/backoff
why: retry.ts is the reliability backbone (backoff, outage notification, give-up) and has no unit test at all, while its neighbor circuit-breaker.ts does. A retry bug either hammers a failing provider or gives up on a transient blip.

acceptance: Panel shows an undo button that is disabled with nothing to undo, enabled after an assistant edit, and restores the files with a feed confirmation
steps: Add an undo button to the panel header in chatView.ts using the existing icon-button styling, disabled when there is nothing to undo
Route the button's webview message to the existing undoLast command handler in the host
Show a one-line confirmation in the feed after an undo (which files were restored)
Add a host test asserting the button posts the undo message and the disabled state tracks undo availability
tests: test/unit/vscode-chat-view.test.ts (new): button posts undo, disabled state, confirmation shown
title: Visible undo button in the chat panel
why: undoLast exists as a command but is only reachable from the palette/title menu, so most users never find it. Undoing the last message's edits is a core recovery action and deserves a visible button next to the composer.

acceptance: Six new bindings work when the chat panel is focused and do nothing elsewhere; Settings lists them; package.json validates
steps: Add keybindings in package.json for pause, resume, stop, new chat, undo last, and model picker, with when-clauses restricting them to the omnexx chat view being focused
Add a Shortcuts section to the Settings page (settings.ts) listing every binding in a table with its action
Pick bindings that do not collide with VS Code defaults on macOS and Windows/Linux
Add a test that parses package.json and asserts every keybinding references a command that exists in contributes.commands
tests: test/unit/vscode-package.test.ts (new): every keybinding maps to a contributed command; JSON parses
title: Keyboard shortcuts for pause/stop/new chat/undo/model, plus a shortcuts help section
why: The extension has only 2 keybindings (focus chat, show history). Cline/Claude Code users drive everything from the keyboard; pausing or stopping a run today requires reaching for the mouse while the model is mid-stream.

acceptance: `omnexx doctor` completes within ~15 s even with a black-holed network, reporting each stalled check as timed out
steps: Add an AbortSignal.timeout (10 s) to every fetch in the doctor network checks
On timeout, report the check as failed with a 'timed out after 10s' message instead of hanging
Apply the same timeout to the provider endpoint probes doctor performs
Add tests with a stubbed fetch that never resolves, asserting doctor completes and reports the timeout
tests: test/unit/cli/doctor.test.ts: never-resolving fetch reports timeout; normal checks unchanged
title: Add timeouts to doctor's network checks
why: doctor's network checks call globalThis.fetch with no explicit timeout, so `omnexx doctor` can hang indefinitely on a stalled network. A diagnostics command must never hang.

acceptance: Cap enforcement, daily rollover, and balance arithmetic are asserted with exact numbers; no I/O in tests
steps: Write tests for recording spend per provider, cap enforcement (block at cap, allow below), and per-day rollover
Cover concurrent-record ordering and the zero/negative spend edge cases
Use in-memory storage only, no filesystem or network
Assert exact balances after a sequence of mixed records and resets
tests: test/unit/providers/quota-ledger.test.ts (new): record, cap block/allow, rollover, exact balances
title: Unit tests for the per-provider quota ledger
why: The quota ledger tracks per-provider spend against caps: the user's money. It has no tests, so a ledger bug could either overspend or falsely block a run.

acceptance: Exact dollar amounts asserted for known models; unknown price yields 'unknown'; zero tokens yields $0.00
steps: Write tests for known model prices (input/output/cache rates) with exact expected dollar amounts
Cover unknown-price models (must yield 'unknown', never a silent zero or a crash) and zero-token edge cases
Cover cached-token pricing separately from fresh tokens
Assert rounding behavior matches what the panel displays
tests: test/unit/providers/pricing.test.ts (new): known prices exact, unknown-price handling, zero tokens, cache rates
title: Unit tests for token pricing
why: pricing.ts turns token counts into dollars shown in the panel and used by budget enforcement. Untested pricing means the spend numbers users trust could be wrong.

acceptance: `omnexx mcp test` against a hanging server fails within ~20 s naming the handshake step; success output unchanged
steps: Add a 15 s timeout to the mcp test probe covering spawn, handshake, and tools/list
On timeout or failure, print which step failed and the last line of server stderr when available
Keep the success output identical so scripts parsing it do not break
Add tests with a stubbed server that hangs at handshake, asserting a timeout error naming the step
tests: test/unit/cli/mcp-command.test.ts: hanging server times out with step named; success path unchanged
title: Add a timeout to mcp test and report the failing step
why: No timeout was found on the mcp test probe calls, so `omnexx mcp test <name>` can hang forever on a wedged server, and when it fails the error does not say which step (spawn, handshake, tools/list) failed.

acceptance: Arrow keys move between tabs, aria-selected tracks the active tab, loading shows a skeleton, tab switches are announced
steps: Add left/right arrow-key navigation between cockpit tabs with roving tabindex, and sync aria-selected/aria-expanded on switch
Show a skeleton preview (grey blocks matching the preview layout) while the page loads instead of a blank panel
Announce tab switches via aria-live so screen readers follow
Add tests asserting arrow keys move focus, aria attributes update, and the skeleton appears during load
tests: test/unit/vscode-browser-cockpit.test.ts (new): arrow-key nav, aria sync, skeleton on load
title: Keyboard-accessible browser cockpit tabs with loading skeleton
why: The browser cockpit tabs use role=tablist but have no arrow-key navigation and no aria-expanded sync, and the preview shows a blank panel while loading. Keyboard users and screen-reader users get a degraded diagnostics experience.

acceptance: No providers yields an empty state with an add-provider button; loading still shows the loading text; models list unchanged when present
steps: Detect the empty case (no providers, or providers with no models) and render an empty state instead of the loading placeholder
Include a one-line explanation and a primary button that opens the add-provider form
Keep the existing loading placeholder for the genuinely-loading case
Add tests asserting the empty state renders with the button and the loading state still renders while fetching
tests: test/unit/vscode-model-picker.test.ts (new): empty state with button, loading state preserved
title: Dedicated empty state for the model picker when no providers are configured
why: With no providers configured the picker shows 'Loading models from your providers…' and then goes blank. A first-run user has no idea what to do next; the fix is a one-screen empty state with a single action.

acceptance: Crash shows 'chat server crashed' with the stderr tail; exhaustion shows a restart button; clean stop shows no error banner
steps: Track the exit reason in chatProcess.ts: clean shutdown vs crash (non-zero exit) vs restart exhaustion (3 restarts in 60 s)
Surface the reason plus the stderr tail in the banner via the existing error channel, with a 'Restart chat' action for the exhausted case
Keep the existing restart behavior and caps unchanged
Add tests asserting each exit reason produces the right banner text and the restart action appears only when restarts are exhausted
tests: test/unit/vscode-chat-process.test.ts (new): crash vs clean vs exhausted banners
title: Distinguish chat-server crash from shutdown and show the last error
why: When chat-server dies the panel shows only a generic banner, even though chatProcess.ts already keeps the last 2000 chars of stderr and restarts up to 3x/min. Users cannot tell a crash from a clean stop, or what broke.

acceptance: Splitting, rolling-wave, cap, and degenerate inputs asserted with exact milestone counts; no model calls
steps: Write tests for milestone splitting (one large milestone becomes bounded smaller ones), rolling-wave expansion (later milestones stay coarse until their turn), and the milestone cap
Cover the degenerate inputs: empty goal, single-step goal, and a goal that is already a milestone list
Use pure in-memory plan fixtures, no model calls
Assert exact milestone counts and ordering
tests: test/unit/agent/planner.test.ts (new): split, rolling-wave, cap, empty/single-step goals
title: Unit tests for planner milestone expansion
why: The planner drives every run (milestone splitting, rolling-wave expansion) and has only integration coverage. A planner regression produces bad plans that waste whole runs before anyone notices.

acceptance: All symbol kinds indexed with correct spans; re-index after edit is correct; malformed TS degrades gracefully
steps: Write tests indexing small TS fixtures: functions, classes, methods, interfaces, and exports are found with correct line spans
Cover incremental re-index after an edit (changed symbol updates, deleted symbol disappears)
Cover malformed TS (index must not throw; it reports the file as unparseable)
Assert outline output lists symbols in source order
tests: test/unit/tools/symbol-ts.test.ts (new): symbol kinds, re-index, malformed input, ordering
title: Unit tests for the TypeScript symbol index and outline tools
why: The swe-mode AST tools (symbol index, outline) are how workers read code without dumping whole files, and they have no tests while read-symbol and test-digest do. A broken index silently degrades every swe run to full-file reads.

acceptance: Typing /d, /r, /p, /m in the composer suggests /diff, /report, /plan, /model first; each runs its action
steps: Add /diff, /report, /plan, and /model to the COMMANDS list in suggest.ts with one-line descriptions matching the CLI help text
Wire each command in suggestBox.ts to its existing action (diff view, report generation, plan view, model picker)
Ensure ranking prefers exact prefix matches so /d finds /diff first
Add tests asserting the four commands exist, rank correctly, and trigger the right action
tests: test/unit/vscode-suggest.test.ts (new): commands present, prefix ranking, action wiring
title: Slash-command parity in the panel: /diff /report /plan /model
why: The TUI roadmap lists /run /stop /pause /resume /plan /diff /report /model, but the panel's slash list (suggest.ts COMMANDS) is missing several of them. Panel users cannot reach the most useful run commands without typing full sentences.

acceptance: Each card shows a status dot; error cards show the last error; test button spins then reports the result
steps: Add a status dot to each MCP card in mcpCards.ts (connected / error / unknown) fed by the existing server state in mcp.ts
Show the last error message under the card when status is error, truncated to one line with a title tooltip for the full text
Give the test button a spinner while probing and a success/error result that persists until the next test
Add tests asserting status dots render per state, errors display truncated, and the test button shows spinner then result
tests: test/unit/vscode-mcp.test.ts (new): status dots, error display, test-button states
title: MCP server cards show live status, last error, and test feedback
why: The MCP UI lists servers but gives no live status, so a broken server looks identical to a healthy one until a run fails mid-task. A status dot plus the last error turns a silent failure into a visible one.

acceptance: Inspector lists per-file tokens sorted descending with a correct total; removing a file updates the total immediately
steps: Add a token estimate column per context file in inspector.ts using the existing token-estimation helper
Sort files by token cost descending by default and show the total at the top
Add a remove button per file that drops it from context and refreshes the totals
Add tests asserting totals sum correctly, sorting order, and removal updates the total
tests: test/unit/vscode-inspector.test.ts (new): totals, sorting, removal updates total
title: Context inspector shows per-file token cost and remove-from-context
why: The inspector shows what the model sees but not what each file costs, so users cannot find the file eating their context budget. Per-file tokens plus a one-click remove turns the inspector into a budget tool.

acceptance: Budget shows normal below 80%, amber at 80-94%, red at 95%+; hint appears in warning states; exact boundary behavior tested
steps: Add warning states to the token budget display in stats.ts: amber at 80%, red at 95%, with the remaining tokens shown in both states
Add a one-line hint in the warning state ('compact context or raise the budget')
Keep the normal state visually unchanged below 80%
Add tests asserting the correct state at 0%, 79%, 80%, 94%, 95%, and 100% usage
tests: test/unit/vscode-stats.test.ts (new): boundary cases 79/80/94/95/100%
title: Token budget warnings at 80% and 95% in Live Stats
why: The Live Stats card shows the token budget but never warns before it runs out, so runs die at the budget wall mid-cycle. Two thresholds with distinct styling give users time to act.

acceptance: Both modes show descriptions; switching mid-run asks for confirmation; switching idle applies instantly
steps: Add a one-line description under each mode in domain.ts (swe: strict gates for code; general: artifact-oriented, flexible gates)
When a run is active, show a confirm dialog before applying a mode change, naming the current and target modes
Keep the switch instant and unconfirmed when no run is active
Add tests asserting descriptions render and the confirm appears only during an active run
tests: test/unit/vscode-domain.test.ts (new): descriptions, confirm-when-active, instant-when-idle
title: Work Mode selector explains each mode and confirms mid-run switches
why: The swe/general selector is a bare pill with no explanation, and switching mid-run silently changes verification gates. A one-line description plus a confirm dialog prevents accidental mode changes that invalidate a run's guarantees.

acceptance: No helpers shows the explanatory card with a working button; active helpers show elapsed time; header always visible
steps: Render an empty card in crew.ts when there are no crew members, with one line explaining helpers and a button that opens the run options
Show per-helper elapsed time on each crew card when helpers exist
Keep the section header visible in both states
Add tests asserting the empty card renders with the button and elapsed time appears on active cards
tests: test/unit/vscode-crew.test.ts (new): empty card, button, elapsed time on cards
title: Crew section shows an explanatory empty card instead of hiding
why: When no helpers are running the crew section hides entirely, so the swarm view looks broken rather than idle. An empty card that explains what crew members are and how to add one turns a blank space into an invitation.

acceptance: Every documented outcome maps to its code; unknown outcomes fall back to 1; setExit wiring asserted
steps: Write tests asserting each documented outcome maps to its code (ok 0, needs-human 2, budget 3, stopped 4, error 1)
Cover the mapping function for unknown/undefined outcomes (must fall back to 1, never 0)
Cover the setExit wiring: a needs-human outcome sets process exit code 2
Keep the suite dependency-free and fast
tests: test/unit/cli/exit-codes.test.ts (new): all five codes, unknown fallback, setExit wiring
title: Unit tests for CLI exit codes
why: exit-codes.ts defines the contract scripts rely on (0 ok, 2 needs-human, 3 budget, 4 stopped, 1 error) and is explicitly untested. A wrong exit code makes automation misread run outcomes.

acceptance: `omnexx init --yes` over an existing config leaves a timestamped backup and prints its path; identical content writes no backup
steps: Before writing, check whether omnexx.toml exists; if it does, copy it to omnexx.toml.bak-<timestamp> and print the backup path
Keep the existing ask-first behavior for interactive init unchanged
Skip the backup when the existing file is byte-identical to what would be written
Add tests asserting the backup is created, named with a timestamp, and skipped for identical content
tests: test/unit/cli/init.test.ts: backup created, timestamped name, skipped when identical
title: init --yes backs up an existing omnexx.toml instead of overwriting it
why: init --yes writes omnexx.toml without asking, and today it can silently destroy a hand-tuned config (including a general-mode domain setting). A timestamped backup costs three lines and removes the data-loss footgun.

acceptance: Bad run id errors with the id plus a list of active runs; missing run errors with the listing; valid steer still works
steps: In steer.ts, look up the target run (explicit --run or the current folder's active run) before writing the note
If the run does not exist, fail with a UsageError naming the id and listing the active run ids in this folder
If no run is active and no --run is given, print the same listing instead of a bare error
Add tests for missing run, typo'd id with listing, and the happy path
tests: test/unit/cli/steer.test.ts (new): missing run, typo with listing, happy path
title: steer validates the target run exists before accepting the note
why: steer appends a steering note mid-run, but a typo'd run id today either fails cryptically or silently drops the note. Validating up front and listing nearby run ids turns a lost instruction into a caught typo.

acceptance: Malformed pairs and unknown keys error naming the pair and listing valid keys; valid pairs still apply
steps: Validate each --set pair in connect.ts: reject missing '=', empty key, or empty value with a UsageError naming the offending pair
For a known connector, check the key against that connector's accepted keys and list them in the error when unknown
Keep the success path and output identical
Add tests for malformed pairs, unknown keys (with listing), and the happy path
tests: test/unit/cli/connect.test.ts: malformed pair, unknown key with listing, happy path
title: connect --set validates KEY=VALUE pairs and lists valid keys on error
why: connect --set takes KEY=VALUE pairs, but a malformed pair or an unknown key fails with a generic error. Naming the valid keys for that connector in the error message is the difference between a fixable typo and a docs hunt.

acceptance: `omnexx providers catalog --free` lists only free providers with a count; unfiltered output unchanged
steps: Add a --free flag to the catalog subcommand in providers.ts, filtering to providers marked free in the catalog data
Keep the default (unfiltered) output identical
Show the count of free providers in the header line when filtering
Add tests asserting the filter returns only free providers and the unfiltered list is unchanged
tests: test/unit/cli/providers-catalog.test.ts: free-only results, count line, unfiltered unchanged
title: providers catalog gains a --free filter
why: The provider catalog lists 75+ providers with no way to filter to free ones, which is the first question every new user asks (and the documented free/local-models story). A one-flag filter makes the catalog usable.

acceptance: Hanging probe fails within ~35 s; each failure class prints its own actionable reason; success output unchanged
steps: Add a 30 s timeout to the models test probe in models.ts
Classify failures in the output: auth (check your key), network/timeout (check connectivity), unknown model ref (check the ref spelling)
Keep the success output identical
Add tests with stubbed probes for each failure class and the timeout case
tests: test/unit/cli/models-test.test.ts (new): timeout, auth, network, unknown-ref classes
title: Add a timeout and clear failure reason to models test
why: models test probes a model endpoint with no timeout, so a hung provider hangs the command, and failures do not distinguish auth errors from network errors from bad model refs. Users waste cycles re-running a command that will never return.

acceptance: Non-https URLs and invalid names fail at add time with the rule named; valid adds unchanged
steps: Validate the URL in agent-cards.ts: require https (or http for localhost) and reject anything else with a UsageError
Validate the --name value: reject empty, dash-only, and over-long names (reuse the sanitization rules from #300) with a message naming the rule
Keep the success path identical
Add tests for bad schemes, bad names, and the happy path
tests: test/unit/cli/agent-cards.test.ts: bad scheme, bad names, happy path
title: agent-cards add validates the URL and name up front
why: agent-cards add accepts any URL and name, and bad input only fails later at import time (the recent #300 name-sanitization fix shows the area is fragile). Validating at add time with a clear error saves a confusing failure later.

acceptance: Second identical search is instant and marked cached; --refresh re-fetches; expired cache re-fetches
steps: Cache search results on disk under the user's cache dir with a 1 h TTL in skills-market.ts
Add --refresh to bypass the cache and re-fetch
Print '(cached)' in the header when serving from cache
Add tests asserting the second identical search serves cache, --refresh re-fetches, and expired entries re-fetch
tests: test/unit/cli/skills-market.test.ts (new): cache hit, refresh bypass, expiry re-fetch
title: Cache skills-market search results with a TTL and --refresh
why: Every skills-market search hits the network, so repeated searches are slow and fail offline. A short TTL cache with an explicit refresh flag makes the common case instant without ever serving stale data silently.

acceptance: Bad sources fail before downloading with the class named; download/install failures name their stage; success unchanged
steps: Classify the source in skills.ts before downloading: local path (must exist), URL (must be http(s)), or registry id (must match the id pattern)
Report failures with the stage named: 'could not resolve source', 'download failed', 'install failed', each with the underlying reason
Keep the success path identical
Add tests for each bad-source class and each failure stage with stubbed I/O
tests: test/unit/cli/skills-command.test.ts: bad source classes, failure stages, happy path
title: skills add validates the source and reports download failures clearly
why: skills add takes a source (path, URL, or registry id) and a bad one fails deep in the download with an unhelpful error. Classifying the source first and reporting which stage failed (resolve, download, install) makes the failure actionable.

acceptance: `omnexx service install --dry-run` prints the unit file and writes nothing; real install unchanged
steps: In service.ts, make --dry-run print the full unit/agent file contents to stdout and write nothing
Include the resolved binary path, working directory, and the resume-all command in the printed file
Exit 0 after printing; keep real install behavior unchanged
Add tests asserting dry-run writes no files, prints the unit with correct paths, and exits 0
tests: test/unit/cli/service.test.ts (new): dry-run prints unit, writes nothing, exit 0
title: service install --dry-run prints the unit file it would write
why: service install writes a systemd unit or launchd agent, and today the only way to see what it will write is to install it. A dry-run that prints the exact file (with paths and resume command) lets users verify before committing to a background service.

acceptance: Rotation preserves all events in order across the boundary with no gaps/dupes; segment count capped; tests use a tiny threshold
steps: Write tests with a tiny rotation threshold (injectable, not the 50 MB constant): fill past the threshold and assert the old segment is preserved and the new segment continues
Assert reads across the boundary return events in order with no gaps or duplicates
Assert the rotation keeps at most the configured number of segments
Use a temp dir, no real 50 MB files
tests: test/unit/core/events.test.ts (new): rotation preserves order, no gaps/dupes, segment cap
title: Unit tests for event-log rotation across the boundary
why: Event logs rotate at 50 MB but rotation is untested, and long multi-day runs are the product's core promise. If rotation drops events or breaks logs --events/--cmd reads, run history silently corrupts.

acceptance: Judge errors degrade to no-opinion; judge verdicts never override gate outcomes in either direction; unconfigured judge is a no-op
steps: Write tests asserting a judge failure (throw, timeout, malformed verdict) degrades to 'no opinion' and the run continues
Assert a judge 'fail' verdict never overrides a passing gate, and a judge 'pass' never overrides a failing gate
Cover the endpoint-unavailable path (no judge configured) as a clean no-op
Use stubbed judges only, no model calls
tests: test/unit/judge/fail-open.test.ts (new): error degrades, verdict never overrides gate, unconfigured no-op
title: Unit tests for judge fail-open behavior
why: The judge is advisory, but its fail-open guarantee (it never overrides gates) is load-bearing: a judge bug that blocks a good run or approves a bad one breaks the trust model. Only judge.test.ts exists; fail-open.ts itself is untested.

acceptance: Spawn failure, early exit, malformed lines, and EOF each produce a clear error and a clean close; happy path resolves
steps: Write tests with a stubbed child process: spawn failure reports 'could not start server' with the command, early exit reports the exit code and stderr tail
Cover malformed JSON lines from the server (skipped with a warning, connection stays up) and EOF mid-request (request fails, transport closes cleanly)
